correctness.rationale: For coalition type counts (p,q,r), direct pair counting gives half-cost [p(q+r)u+r(p+q)v]/(p+q+r-1). Positive reciprocal weights for two sorted candidates reduce the theorem to w1*X+w2*Y >= 1. On each fixed-size allocation plane the weighted sum is concave, hence minimizes at a vertex with at most one type split; checking the endpoint cases (including homogeneous singletons and the grand coalition) proves the bound for arbitrary positive a,b,c, u,v. Independently enumerated 77,004 exact-rational split/gap comparisons over 216 type-multiplicity profiles and four gap ratios, all agreeing with the analytic formula. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove arbitrary multiplicities.
residual_risks: Finite tests corroborate but do not replace the analytic infinite/domain-general proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 original formulates the freely-sized two-coalition sortedness conjecture for the average-distance metric hedonic game and proves a concave coefficient decomposition, but the inspected v2 proof and appendix do not give this closed three-distinct-type exact optimum. Fixed-size unsorted counterexamples address a different feasible set. This is a bounded natural subcase with explicit cost, not a claim to settle the four-or-more-type conjecture.
